# Draft:Anoushka Talwar

----
Anoushka Talwar is an American student, activist, and digital media creator known for her early public service work supporting families with premature babies. She gained national attention as a teenager after founding a project to place reading libraries in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) across Georgia. Her initiative has been recognized by major news outlets including CNN, Business Insider, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, and People Magazine, and has been featured on several radio stations across the United States.
Talwar was born in Cincinnati, Ohio, and raised in Georgia. She developed a strong interest in helping others from a young age, adopting a vegetarian lifestyle in the seventh grade due to concerns for animal welfare. As of 2025, she is pursuing higher education at the University of Georgia, where she remains actively involved in advocacy and innovation.
Talwar’s NICU library initiative began as a Girl Scout Silver Award project. Inspired by her own experiences as a premature infant, she sought to support parent-infant bonding through early reading. Her program involved organizing book drives and placing donated children's books in NICU units across Georgia hospitals. The effort has been spotlighted in national news outlets and inspired similar programs elsewhere.
In addition to her community service, Talwar has cultivated a strong digital presence. Her TikTok account has amassed over 300,000 followers, and her YouTube videos have garnered millions of views. She uses these platforms to raise awareness about social issues, mental health, and daily life as a college student and creator.
In 2022, Talwar interned with Georgia State Senator Sheikh Rahman, gaining first-hand experience in government and civic engagement. She has expressed interest in founding a startup and is currently developing a nonprofit organization aimed at youth empowerment and innovation.
Talwar is known for her compassion-driven approach to activism. She is a lifelong animal lover and has adopted two cats. Her personal philosophy centers on making a positive impact and being remembered for meaningful contributions. She has stated that one of her goals is to “make a mark” during her time at the University of Georgia and to honor the support of her family through service and entrepreneurship.
